To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a novel method for maintaining adult porcine enteroid stem cells in vitro.
we developed a novel method that maintains adult porcine enteroid stem cells in culture and that allows their successful passaging and genetic manipulation.
we have developed an efficient and reliable method for the long-term maintenance of porcine enterocytes and crypt stem cells in vitro.   1
In summary, our research is concerned with
the establishment of a porcine model for the in vitro expansion of intestinal stem cells and their subsequent use for transplantation.
a culture system for porcine enterocytes and stem cells.

the establishment and characterization of a novel porcine intestinal stem cell culture system that will facilitate the development of porcine models of intestinal epithelial cell regeneration and transplantation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this is the first report of the isolation, culture, and genetic manipulation of porcine ISCs.

we present a novel and robust method for the culture of porcine intestinal epithelial crypts that can be used as a platform for the study of ISC biology, the development of novel therapies for short bowel syndrome, and as a model to investigate the potential of porcine ISCs for transplantation.
the authors have developed a novel culture system that maintains juvenile and adult pig intestinal crypts long term in culture, and these crypts can be serially passaged.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we developed a method to grow adult porcine enteroid cultures that can be passaged and transgene expressing.
we established a novel culture method to support porcine crypt cell proliferation and differentiation, and we demonstrated the feasibility of genetic manipulation of porcine ISCs.
we have developed a culture system that can maintain juvenile and adult porine crypt cells long term in culture, and we were able to passaged and transduce these cells by lentiviral vector.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have developed a novel culture system that maintains adult porcine jejunal crypts in culture for up to 3 weeks.
we have developed an efficient culture system to maintain porcine crypt stem cells long-term.
we have established a method to maintain adult porcine ISCs in culture, which is essential for future studies on porcine stem cell-based therapies.
